book_title: Dad Jokes from Late in the Patriarchy
subject_line: The punchlines in Dad Jokes from Late in the Patriarchy
email_body:
Dear Amorak,

The title Dad Jokes from Late in the Patriarchy has stayed with me; it promises humor and reckoning in the same breath, which seems hard to hold steady across a whole book. I'd love to ask how you decide when a joke in a poem should land and when it should curdle, and whether co-writing Poetry: A Writer's Guide and Anthology with W. Todd Kaneko changed how you think about that. The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication. Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Dad Jokes from Late in the Patriarchy (Sundress 2021) and Bloomsbury textbook with Kaneko (2nd ed. 2024), per Sundress blog/Poetry Foundation; directs BGSU CW program; email seen in search result (BGSU faculty page).

Dear Sharona,

Invisible Beasts sits somewhere between novel and field guide, with Sophie, an amateur naturalist, cataloguing creatures most people can't see, from truth bats to beanie sharks, and arguing that humans are the most invisible beasts of all. I'd be curious to hear how you invented the biology of these animals, and whether the bestiary form came first or grew out of Sophie's voice. subject_line: The family curse of falling in Defenestrate
email_body:
Dear Renée,

Defenestrate traces a family's belief that it is cursed with falls back to a great-great-grandfather in nineteenth-century Prague who pushed a stonemason out a window, then follows the twins Marta and Nick to that same city. I'd like to ask what drew you to Prague and its long history of defenestrations, and how you balanced the curse as family myth against the very real fall Nick suffers. The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. subject_line: The winter quarters of The Circus in Winter
email_body:
Dear Cathy,

The Circus in Winter builds a century of linked stories around a traveling circus wintering in a town modeled on Peru, Indiana, where you grew up, and then the book had a second life when Ball State students adapted it into a musical that eventually reached Goodspeed. I'd love to ask what it was like to tell those students to change whatever they needed, and whether watching your characters sing changed how you see them. The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. book_title: Beep: Inside the Unseen World of Baseball for the Blind
subject_line: Beep baseball, from Indy to Senegal
email_body:
Dear David,

Beep follows teams like the Indy Thunder and Taiwan Homerun, and players such as Ethan Johnston, through a game where everyone but the pitcher is visually impaired; I gather it took about three years and roughly a hundred interviews. Since then you have helped bring beep baseball to Senegal. I'd love to ask how the book's reporting led to that trip, and how writing about a sport played by sound changed the way you write scenes. The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. subject_line: One foot in myth: the Trung sisters in Bronze Drum
email_body:
Dear Phong,

Bronze Drum takes the Trung sisters, two daughters of a Vietnamese lord in Au Lac under Han Chinese rule, and follows them from their father's execution toward rebellion. You've described the book as having one foot in history and one foot in myth. I'd love to ask how you decided where legend should take over from the historical record, and how you shaped two sisters with such different temperaments so that neither eclipses the other. The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.
